name: Udawalawe
line: Open grassland and elephants, and a good first safari for children.

image.alt: Elephants grazing on open grassland under the hills

summary: Open grassland around a reservoir, with several hundred elephants and a first safari that almost never disappoints.

intro.heading: Elephants, every time.
paragraphs: Udawalawe is flatter and more open than Yala: grassland and scrub around a large reservoir at the foot of the hills. Several hundred elephants live here, and you are all but certain to see them, often close to the jeep.

That makes it the park we suggest for children and for a first safari. It sits between the hills and the south coast, so it breaks up a long drive, and the elephant transit home beside the park is worth an hour.

mapCaption: Between the hills and the south coast. The other dots are the places we pair it with.

doing.lede: Udawalawe is a half day, not a week. These are the things we build it around.

items.title: An afternoon drive
items.body: Three or four hours in an open jeep, with elephants at the water, buffalo, crocodiles and eagles overhead.

items.title: The elephant transit home
items.body: Orphaned calves are raised here and later released into the park. Feeding time is short, and kept at a distance.

items.title: The reservoir from the dam
items.body: The road along the dam looks out over the water, and elephants often come down to drink below it.

items.title: Birds, for the keen
items.body: Bee-eaters, fish eagles and more than two hundred other species. We can book a guide who cares more about them than the elephants.

gallery.alt: An elephant beside a safari jeep on the grassland
A child in a safari jeep watching an elephant in the long grass

season: Udawalawe has no long closure, and the elephants stay whatever the month. February to August is the driest time, and the easiest for seeing them at the water.
ctaBody: Tell us your dates and we will fit a drive in on the way from the hills to the coast.
